senses.gloss: The thing you aim at when you shoot or throw.
examples: His first arrow fell short of the *mark*.
Her guess about the price was close to the *mark*.
The critics' complaints were wide of the *mark*.

senses.gloss: A sign or feature that shows the presence or quality of something.
examples: The flags were lowered as a *mark* of respect.
Patience is the *mark* of a good teacher.
Hand stitching is a *mark* of quality in a boot.

senses.gloss: A particular point on a scale or in a stretch of time.
examples: Donations passed the million-dollar *mark* last night.
He was pulled from the game just before the ten-minute *mark*.
Water rose above the flood *mark* on the wall.

senses.gloss: An object or sign put in place to show where something is.
examples: A stone *marker* shows where the trail crosses the river.
Mile *markers* count down to the state line.
The family finally put a *marker* on the grave.

senses.gloss: A sign in the body or in data that shows something is present.
examples: The blood test looks for *markers* of inflammation.
Researchers found a genetic *marker* linked to the disease.
Vocabulary size is a rough *marker* of reading ability.

senses.gloss: A place where sellers set up stalls to sell food and goods.
examples: We buy eggs at the farmers *market* on Saturdays.
The Christmas *market* takes over the whole square.
She sells honey at three *markets* around the county.

senses.gloss: The group of people who might buy a particular product.
examples: Teenagers are the main *market* for the game.
There's no *market* for typewriters anymore.
The company is trying to reach an older *market*.

senses.gloss: An official who directs people at an event or enforces safety rules.
examples: The fire *marshal* said the room could hold sixty people.
*Marshals* in orange vests kept the race course clear.
A retired astronaut was grand *marshal* of the parade.

senses.gloss: Someone who makes a show of suffering in order to get sympathy.
examples: Don't play the *martyr* — I offered to help twice.
He cleans up after everyone and then acts like a *martyr*.
She's such a *martyr* about having to work weekends.

senses.gloss: A covering worn over the face to hide or protect it.
examples: The robber wore a ski *mask*.
Every kid in the parade had a *mask* on.
Welders wear a *mask* to protect their eyes.

senses.gloss: A cream or sheet spread on the face as a beauty treatment.
examples: She puts on a clay *mask* every Sunday night.
The facial ends with a warm *mask*.
These sheet *masks* are supposed to hydrate your skin.

senses.gloss: A false outward appearance that hides someone's real feelings.
examples: He listened behind a *mask* of polite interest.
Her cheerfulness was a *mask* for real worry.
The *mask* slipped and he finally yelled at us.

senses.gloss: The original recording that all copies are made from.
examples: The studio lost the *master* of their first album.
They cleaned up the old tapes and cut a new *master*.
Every record was pressed from a single *master*.

senses.gloss: A thick tangled mass of hair, grass, or roots.
examples: The dog came home with *mats* of burrs in his fur.
A *mat* of dead leaves covered the drain.
Roots form a dense *mat* just under the soil.

senses.gloss: A short stick that makes a flame when you strike it.
examples: He struck a *match* and lit the candle.
There's a box of *matches* above the stove.
The wind blew out three *matches* in a row.

senses.gloss: Something that is the same as another thing or goes well with it.
examples: The lab found a *match* for the fingerprints.
That scarf is a perfect *match* for your coat.
The search came back with no *matches*.

senses.gloss: Someone who is equal to another in strength or skill.
examples: The rookie was no *match* for the champion.
In an argument she's more than a *match* for him.
After forty years of winning, he finally met his *match*.

senses.gloss: An officer on a ship who ranks below the captain.
examples: The first *mate* took the wheel at midnight.
He worked two seasons as a *mate* on a fishing boat.
The captain and the *mate* argued about the route.

senses.gloss: One of a pair of things that belong together.
examples: I can never find the *mate* to this sock.
One glove turned up, but its *mate* is gone.
The vase lost its *mate* years ago.

senses.gloss: A subject or situation that has to be dealt with.
examples: We'll take up the *matter* at the next meeting.
It's a serious *matter* and the police are involved.
Getting a visa is just a *matter* of paperwork.

senses.gloss: The trouble or problem that someone or something has.
examples: What's the *matter*? You look upset.
Something's the *matter* with the printer again.
There's nothing the *matter* with the car.

senses.gloss: Grain that has been coarsely ground.
examples: Stir the *meal* slowly into boiling salted water.
He works bone *meal* into the soil before planting.
The mill grinds oats into a coarse *meal*.

senses.gloss: The sense of purpose or importance that something gives a person's life.
examples: Volunteering gave her life new *meaning*.
He went looking for *meaning* after the divorce.
The ceremony has deep *meaning* for the whole family.

senses.gloss: A swimming race in which the strokes change from one leg to the next.
examples: She won gold in the 400-meter individual *medley*.
Our team came in second in the *medley* relay.
He swims the breaststroke leg of the *medley*.

senses.gloss: A threatening quality in the way someone looks, sounds, or behaves.
examples: There was real *menace* in his voice.
The music slowly builds a sense of *menace*.
She said it quietly, with a hint of *menace*.

senses.gloss: The list of dishes that a restaurant offers.
examples: Could we see the *menu*, please?
Everything on the lunch *menu* is under twelve dollars.
They print new *menus* every season.

senses.gloss: Something lucky that you are thankful for.
examples: It's a *mercy* nobody was home when the roof came down.
Be grateful for small *mercies*.
That the pain finally stopped was a *mercy*.

senses.gloss: A confused or badly handled situation.
examples: The scheduling system is a complete *mess*.
He made a *mess* of his first semester.
After the layoffs her finances were a *mess*.

senses.gloss: A room where soldiers or sailors eat together.
examples: The recruits lined up outside the *mess* at six.
He ate every meal that year in the officers' *mess*.
Both *messes* were closed for the holiday.

senses.gloss: The main idea that a book, movie, or speech is trying to get across.
examples: The film's *message* is that it's never too late to change.
Her speech had a simple *message*: show up.
The ads send a mixed *message* to kids.

senses.gloss: A loud, heavy style of rock music.
examples: He's been into *metal* since middle school.
The bar books punk and *metal* bands on weekends.
That drummer came out of the *metal* scene.

senses.gloss: A device that measures and records how much of something is used.
examples: The gas *meter* is in the basement.
I fed quarters into the parking *meter*.
A technician comes out once a month to read the *meters*.

senses.gloss: The pattern of rhythm in a line of poetry or a piece of music.
examples: Shakespeare wrote most of his lines in a five-beat *meter*.
The poem breaks its *meter* in the very last line.
The class learned to clap out the *meter*.

senses.gloss: A large city taken together with the suburbs around it.
examples: Half a million people live in the Portland *metro*.
Rents are climbing across the whole *metro*.
The chain has stores in four *metros*.

senses.gloss: A congressional election held halfway through a president's term.
examples: The party lost the House in the *midterms*.
Turnout is lower in a *midterm* than in a presidential year.
Both candidates are already campaigning for the *midterms*.

senses.gloss: A bird or animal that travels to another region with the seasons.
examples: The first *migrants* show up at the feeder in April.
Warblers are long-distance *migrants*.
Storms can blow *migrants* hundreds of miles off course.

senses.gloss: A person of great intelligence.
examples: She was one of the finest *minds* of her generation.
The lab attracts the best young *minds* in the field.
It took a great *mind* to see the pattern at all.

senses.gloss: A person's opinion or intention about something.
examples: She changed her *mind* about going.
He always speaks his *mind* at meetings.
We were of the same *mind* on the budget.

senses.gloss: A deep hole or system of tunnels dug to take coal or metal out of the ground.
examples: His grandfather worked in a coal *mine* for thirty years.
The copper *mine* closed in the 1980s.
Old *mines* run under the hills above town.

senses.gloss: A rich source of something, especially information.
examples: That old census is a *mine* of information.
Her notebooks are a *mine* of ideas.
For a historian the archive is a gold *mine*.

senses.gloss: A substance such as iron or calcium that the body needs in small amounts from food.
examples: Leafy greens are full of vitamins and *minerals*.
The doctor said she was short on one *mineral*.
The label lists every *mineral* added to the cereal.

senses.gloss: A person who is not yet legally an adult.
examples: The bar was fined for serving a *minor*.
Both drivers were *minors*.
As a *minor*, she needed a parent's signature.

senses.gloss: The place where a country's coins are made.
examples: The coin was struck at the Denver *mint*.
The *mint* is releasing a new quarter this year.
Tours of the *mint* sell out weeks ahead.

senses.gloss: A very large amount of money.
examples: That kitchen must have cost a *mint*.
He made a *mint* selling the patent.
They spent a *mint* on the wedding.

senses.gloss: Something wonderful and lucky that seemed impossible.
examples: It's a *miracle* nobody was hurt in that crash.
The country's economic *miracle* lasted twenty years.
Getting four kids out the door on time was a small *miracle*.

senses.gloss: A polite title or form of address for a young or unmarried woman.
examples: *Miss* Parker teaches third grade.
Excuse me, *miss*, you dropped your scarf.
The letter was addressed to *Miss* Alcott.

senses.gloss: An important job or purpose that a person or organization takes on.
examples: Their *mission* is to get books into rural schools.
He's on a *mission* to fix the city's bus routes.
The charity's *mission* statement fits on one line.

senses.gloss: A place run by a religious group to spread its faith or help the poor.
examples: The old Spanish *mission* still holds services.
He slept at a downtown *mission* that winter.
The church supports two *missions* overseas.

senses.gloss: A padded leather glove used to catch a baseball.
examples: The catcher pounded his *mitt* and waited for the pitch.
She oiled her new *mitt* every night.
He caught the line drive in the web of his *mitt*.

senses.gloss: A person's hand, in informal speech.
examples: Get your *mitts* off my fries.
He wiped his *mitts* on his jeans.
Keep your *mitts* to yourself.

senses.gloss: A combination of different qualities, feelings, or kinds of thing.
examples: She watched with a *mixture* of pride and worry.
The block is a *mixture* of old houses and new condos.
His answer was a strange *mixture* of honesty and bluff.

senses.gloss: The value that appears most often in a set of numbers.
examples: The *mode* of the test scores was 85.
In this data set the *mode* and the mean are far apart.
Find the mean, the median, and the *mode*.

senses.gloss: A simplified description of a system, used to explain or predict how it behaves.
examples: Every climate *model* points the same direction.
Their economic *model* failed to predict the crash.
The forecast comes out of a computer *model*.

senses.gloss: A person or thing held up as an excellent example to copy.
examples: He's a *model* of patience with the kids.
The program became a *model* for other cities.
Her grandmother was a *model* of quiet generosity.

senses.gloss: Care not to show too much of the body or attract attention to it.
examples: She pulled the blanket up for *modesty*.
The dress code is about *modesty*, not fashion.
He changed behind a towel to preserve his *modesty*.

senses.gloss: A hard bump of packed snow on a ski slope.
examples: The lower run was covered in *moguls*.
She took the *moguls* fast and never lost her line.
By afternoon the powder had been chopped into *moguls*.

senses.gloss: A fuzzy growth of fungus on damp surfaces or old food.
examples: There's *mold* on the bread again.
Black *mold* was growing behind the shower tile.
The basement smells of damp and *mold*.
